headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in Shenzhen
summary: The White House said on Friday 13 November that Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will hold their first three-way meeting next Thursday, 19 November, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China.
display_body: The White House said on Friday 13 November that Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will hold their first three-way meeting next Thursday, 19 November, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China. White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Trump would raise "the reduction of the number of nuclear weapons in the world", and a US official said the Iran war would be discussed but Ukraine would not, because Washington is running "a completely separate track" with Kyiv and Moscow. Neither Beijing nor Moscow had confirmed the meeting by Saturday morning. Expectations are low: a senior US official told Reuters "we do not expect to get to any kind of agreement". The meeting comes nine months after New START (the last treaty capping US and Russian nuclear warheads) expired in February, after Trump turned down Russia's offer of a one-year extension and asked for a new deal that also covers China.
why: for the first time in more than 50 years, the world's two largest nuclear arsenals have no treaty limits. A meeting that only starts a conversation about arms control would still be the first such talk to include China, whose arsenal is growing fastest.

headline: US floats NATO entry for Donbas pullout
summary: Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks his office published on Saturday 14 November that US negotiators had asked, after the latest round of talks in Abu Dhabi, whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas if it joined NATO.
display_body: Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks his office published on Saturday 14 November that US negotiators had asked, after the latest round of talks in Abu Dhabi, whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas if it joined NATO. On Friday 13 November, EU leaders in Dublin agreed who will speak for Europe in the talks. "This is the first time this question has been raised," Zelensky said. He repeated that Ukraine will not pull its troops out of the part of the eastern region it still holds, and that Ukrainians would be asked to approve any peace deal in a referendum. In Dublin, European Council President António Costa said Europe's negotiating team will be made up of the EU institutions (the Commission and the Council) and the "E5": Germany, France, Italy, Poland and the UK. That compromise sits between smaller states, which wanted the EU's foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas or Costa himself to represent Europe, and Berlin and Rome, which wanted their own negotiators. It is still unclear who would sit at a leaders' table with Trump, Putin and Zelensky. Separately, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told NATO that Poland will stop contributing to PURL (the scheme under which NATO allies buy US weapons for Ukraine) "for now", pointing to its budget deficit.
why: this is the first time Washington has floated NATO membership, which it had treated as off the table, as a trade for the territory Russia demands. At the same time Europe finally has an agreed seat at the table, and one of Ukraine's biggest backers is pulling back from paying for its air defence.

headline: Oil glut returns as Hormuz stays deadly
summary: Global oil supply now exceeds demand for the first time since the Iran war began in February, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly Oil Market Report on Friday 13 November.
display_body: Global oil supply now exceeds demand for the first time since the Iran war began in February, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly Oil Market Report on Friday 13 November. The same day, a UN official told the Security Council that 25 seafarers had been killed in and around the Strait of Hormuz as of 11 November. The IEA says world supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day in October, to 105.4 mb/d, on "lofty Gulf exports" despite continuing attacks on tankers and energy sites, and it expects 2026 demand to fall by 2.7 mb/d as high prices push drivers towards hybrids and electric cars. RFI reports that Gulf exports are back to 74% of pre-war levels and that Brent crude has fallen 18% since the start of the month. At the Security Council meeting, which Bahrain requested, Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Khiari cited International Maritime Organization data showing 134 attacks and other security incidents involving ships, with October the worst month since February. "This should not be mistaken for a return to normality," he said, because shipments are still below pre-war volumes. Gulf states and Iran blamed each other for the insecurity.
why: a market that has moved from shortage to surplus is what is pulling fuel and heating prices down in Europe. But the route those barrels take is no safer, and October was the most dangerous month for crews.

headline: Qatar and Türkiye sign defence pact
summary: Qatar and Türkiye signed a mutual defence agreement in Istanbul on Friday 13 November, at the twelfth meeting of their Supreme Strategic Committee, chaired by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani.
display_body: Qatar and Türkiye signed a mutual defence agreement in Istanbul on Friday 13 November, at the twelfth meeting of their Supreme Strategic Committee, chaired by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. Türkiye's Directorate of Communications listed the "Mutual Defence Agreement" among the documents signed, along with deals on education, consumer protection and conflict mediation. According to the joint communiqué, as reported by Al Jazeera, the two countries commit to a common position against any external armed attack on either of them, to consult each other on threats, and to expand joint exercises and defence-industry cooperation. The communiqué, as reported, does not say what would trigger the pact or what a joint response would look like. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera describe it as a deterrent rather than an offensive alliance.
why: a Gulf state that hosts a large US airbase now also has a defence commitment from a NATO member, a sign that Gulf capitals are looking for security guarantees beyond Washington while the Iran war goes on.

headline: Outage grounds every US departure
summary: A nationwide "ground stop" that halted every departure from US airports for about four hours on Friday 13 November was lifted at 20:15 US Eastern time (02:15 in Switzerland).
display_body: A nationwide "ground stop" that halted every departure from US airports for about four hours on Friday 13 November was lifted at 20:15 US Eastern time (02:15 in Switzerland). By then nearly 6,700 flights had been cancelled, and about 7,500 two hours later. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that "as far as we know, it was not a cyberattack". Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed a telecommunications failure and "an incredibly outdated air traffic control system": "the routers were overloaded", he said, and data mismatches led officials to shut the system down. Duffy has been asking Congress for at least $30 billion to modernise air traffic control. Congress approved $12.5 billion last year to begin the work. Airlines warn it will take days to recover.

headline: Hungary digs up $20m in graft probe
summary: Hungarian investigators found nearly $20 million in hidden cash, some of it buried in forests, during searches on 12 and 13 November, the country's new National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said on Friday 13 November.
display_body: Hungarian investigators found nearly $20 million in hidden cash, some of it buried in forests, during searches on 12 and 13 November, the country's new National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said on Friday 13 November. The money (5.07 billion forints, €2.66 million and $1.26 million) was found in Budapest and three counties, in farm buildings, warehouses, a home and a safe at a secluded location. The searches are part of an investigation into Miklós Seszták, development minister from 2014 to 2018 under Viktor Orbán, who is suspected of taking bribes linked to overpriced second-hand bus purchases and state construction projects. Prime Minister Péter Magyar, whose Tisza party ended Orbán's 16 years in power in April's election, called it the end of the "Fidesz-KDNP mafia". Orbán has accused the new government of using such investigations against its opponents.

headline: South Sudan delays vote to February
summary: South Sudan's National Elections Commission has moved the country's first-ever general election from Tuesday 22 December 2026 to Thursday 11 February 2027, according to a revised calendar reported on Saturday 14 November.
display_body: South Sudan's National Elections Commission has moved the country's first-ever general election from Tuesday 22 December 2026 to Thursday 11 February 2027, according to a revised calendar reported on Saturday 14 November. The commission gave no reason. Radio Tamazuj notes that the new date falls outside the December 2026 deadline set in law. Under the new timetable, voter registration runs from 14 to 28 November, the 45-day campaign from 27 December to 9 February, and any run-off on 12 April 2027. The vote was first due in 2022 and has now been postponed at least three times. In September, President Salva Kiir dissolved the unity government. The UN's human rights commission on South Sudan called that step a "constitutional coup".

headline: Qatar's emir heads to Bern
summary: Qatar's Emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, will make a two-day state visit to Switzerland, the Federal Council announced on Friday 13 November.
display_body: Qatar's Emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, will make a two-day state visit to Switzerland, the Federal Council announced on Friday 13 November. He will be received with military honours on the Federal Square in Bern on Wednesday 18 November. Federal President Guy Parmelin and Federal Councillors Ignazio Cassis, Karin Keller-Sutter and Albert Rösti will hold the official talks. The government says they will cover the economy, financial policy, science, regional conflicts and mediation, and energy supply. On Thursday 19 November, Parmelin and the emir will meet business leaders. The two countries opened embassies only in 2013, and Qatar has since become a significant direct investor in Switzerland and a major exporter of natural gas.
why: the emir arrives in Bern a few days after signing a defence pact with Türkiye (see World). With Gulf gas and Qatari mediation both in play during the Iran war, the energy and "good offices" parts of the agenda are the ones to watch.

headline: Vaud calls budget strike unlawful
summary: Vaud's Conseil d'État said on Thursday 12 November that any strike by the public-sector unions FSF, SSP and SUD over the 2027 budget would be unlawful, and asked state staff not to join one, though it says it does not plan sanctions "for now".
display_body: Vaud's Conseil d'État said on Thursday 12 November that any strike by the public-sector unions FSF, SSP and SUD over the 2027 budget would be unlawful, and asked state staff not to join one, though it says it does not plan sanctions "for now". The statement came the same day the canton's conciliation body formally recorded that talks had failed, which is one of the legal preconditions for a strike. The unions want all the budget cuts the government proposed after voters accepted the so-called "12% initiative" to be withdrawn, with the lost revenue covered instead by one-off income or the canton's reserves. The government argues that the cantonal staff law allows strikes only over working conditions and only when they are proportionate. It says this dispute is about budget policy, which is now in the hands of the Grand Council. It also points out that more than 60% of the CHF 272 million gap will be covered by one-off revenue, and that salaries in the public and para-public sectors will be fully indexed from 1 January 2027.
why: this is the government's legal reading, not a court's. Whether a strike is lawful under the staff law would ultimately be for a court to decide, so the next move is the unions'.

headline: Lausanne tram opens 13 December
summary: The Lausanne–Renens tram will enter commercial service with the national timetable change on Sunday 13 December 2026, after the Federal Office of Transport gave the Lausanne public transport operator (tl) its go-ahead this week, the canton said on Friday 13 November.
display_body: The Lausanne–Renens tram will enter commercial service with the national timetable change on Sunday 13 December 2026, after the Federal Office of Transport gave the Lausanne public transport operator (tl) its go-ahead this week, the canton said on Friday 13 November. An opening celebration on Saturday 5 December will let the public ride the line a week before it starts regular service.

headline: Bern seeks faster airport border checks
summary: Justice Minister Beat Jans met border-control authorities, airlines and airports on Friday 13 November to look at ways to shorten waiting times at airport border checks since the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) began in October 2025.
display_body: Justice Minister Beat Jans met border-control authorities, airlines and airports on Friday 13 November to look at ways to shorten waiting times at airport border checks since the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) began in October 2025. EES records the biometric data and border crossings of non-EU travellers entering the Schengen area. Across Schengen it has logged more than 225 million entries and exits by 90 million travellers in just over a year, and more than 78,000 people have been refused entry. One option under study is a national programme in which eligible non-EU travellers, for example from the UK, register in advance once and then use automatic eGates without questioning at the border.

headline: Federal Council presses army funding
summary: At the Von Wattenwyl talks on Friday 13 November, the Federal Council told the leaders of the governing parties that the planned additional CHF 24 billion for the army, and a fund that is allowed to borrow, are "necessary" to deliver the defence posture it set on 19 June 2026.
display_body: At the Von Wattenwyl talks on Friday 13 November, the Federal Council told the leaders of the governing parties that the planned additional CHF 24 billion for the army, and a fund that is allowed to borrow, are "necessary" to deliver the defence posture it set on 19 June 2026. Without them, it said, its arms-spending plan could not be carried out and the army could not protect the population effectively against the most likely threats. The meeting also covered the 2027–2031 legislative programme and a new national strategy against domestic, sexual and gender-based violence. The government says that strategy is urgent given the "particularly high" number of femicides in 2025.
